purpose: Cut over public package lookup/refs/find authority to the NEW ConfigData Lookup namespace and retire legacy Stage 7/8 Doctor-style selector authority from active package/workflow/runtime surfaces without reopening Stage 0-6 materialization semantics.

legacyAuthorityRetirement.reason: Stage 7/8 artifacts remain frozen historical evidence. CLR7 retires their active orchestration authority rather than deleting completed evidence or reopening their semantics.

ownershipBoundary.packageJsonLookupValidation: Project Tooling ConfigData Lookup workflow explicitly triggers on package.json and the aggregate owner self-test asserts exact lookup/refs/find aliases.

validationImplementation.activeAuthorityScan: Scan package.json and every .github/workflows YAML for legacy Stage 7/8 selector/validator invocation tokens.
validationImplementation.cliParity: Execute npm run lookup/refs/find through NEW package aliases and compare stdout/stderr/exit status to the preserved legacy CLI for representative positive, find, refs, and absent-ID cases.

reviews.detail: scripts/configdata-lookup-cli.mjs remains as preserved parity/historical compatibility reference, but package authority is transferred to tools/configdata-lookup/cli/run.mjs.
Stage 7/8 contracts, libraries, validators and summaries are not physically deleted because they are completed historical evidence; active package/workflow/NEW runtime authority must remain zero.

nextStart: After CLR7 freeze, begin CLR8 final freeze: inventory final ConfigData Lookup authority/runtime/writer surfaces, verify all CLR0-7 predecessor completions and current Project Check routing, then freeze the reset as complete without reopening Stage 0-6 semantics.
reopenConditions: package lookup/refs/find stops resolving to tools/configdata-lookup/cli/run.mjs or diverges from preserved CLI behavior.
Any active package script or workflow begins invoking legacy ConfigData Lookup Stage 7/8 selector authority.
NEW ConfigData Lookup runtime imports Stage 7/8 Doctor-style selection logic.
Stage 0-6 materialization semantics or generated data are changed as part of the cutover.
Project Check or the dedicated ConfigData Lookup workflow no longer validates the CLR7 cutover contract.
